agree.reason: This owner's cousin does her books for $600 a year and she's fond of him, and the page never speaks to that, so $199 a month looks like a big new cost with no reason to drop someone she trusts.

honest.reason: Most claims match the brief, but 'One of them saved $800' states as fact what the client only reported, and the 'if you change nothing' section assumes the reader's books are messy, which the brief doesn't support.

works_the_facts.reason: Raw facts are repeated without working them out: no yearly cost ($2,388), no retention rate (31 of 33, and both who left had sold), no on-time record (9 of 12 months), and no share of clients who saved at tax time (9 of 31).

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is pictured as an accountant billing to untangle messy books, but this reader's real alternative is a cousin charging $600 a year, and the page never compares against that.

qualification.reason: The admission of three missed deadlines comes with no consequence the reader could check, such as a free month when the 10th is missed, so the hedge is candid but gives her nothing to hold onto.

objections.reason: The central objection, 'my cousin already does this cheaply', goes unmet, and the page brings up the price rise without saying why it happened (payroll was added), so it raises a doubt it doesn't settle.

fit.reason: It is a sales page of about 350 words with clear sections and ends with a button to book the call, as the brief asked.
